user_prompt: What is the effect of indicated interventions (interventions targeting young people up to age 25 who are already showing early signs or symptoms of risk, such as existing suicidal ideation or self-harm history — as distinct from universal interventions delivered to everyone regardless of risk, or selective interventions targeting at-risk groups who are not yet symptomatic), compared with control, on suicidal ideation measured immediately at the end of the intervention (postintervention), in education settings?  This is specifically the POSTINTERVENTION timepoint — do not include short-term (1-3 months), medium-term (4-12 months), or longest-follow-up suicidal ideation measurements; those are separate outcomes in this review.  Note on scale direction: a LOWER suicidal ideation score means a BETTER outcome — code the effect size so a positive value means the indicated intervention reduced suicidal ideation more than control.  Note on multi-arm trials: if a trial has more than one indicated-intervention arm compared against a single shared control group (e.g. two different intervention types tested against one common control), extract each intervention arm as its own separate row against that same shared control — do not merge the two intervention arms together, and do not pick only one and discard the other.  If a study does not report the number of participants in each group separately (only a total), and the trial was randomized, you may assume an even 50/50 split between groups unless the paper states otherwise — note this assumption explicitly when you make it.
